Boundaries. Every printed part the scheme prices separately is its own task:
Part One (i), (ii) and lettered (ii)(a)/(b) true/false items; Part Two A-part
romans; every B/C task and every option. A part whose rows share ONE printed
instruction and ONE closed answer pool (the Part One matching and location
tables, A-part "Name each of the features labelled A, B, C and D") stays one
task with a criterion per scheme row: the rows have no printed address of
their own and could only be separated by writing new prompts. The scheme's
roman/letter rows follow the printed table rows; this was checked visually
for Q1-Q6 and Q9 (e.g. Q2 Oxbow lake=C, River braiding=B, Lateral
moraines=D, Fjord=A against the four photographs).

Tariffs are read off the scheme: an "a + b marks" line is one criterion of
a+b with partial a; "n x SRPs" is n SRPs at 2 marks; sketch features are
"shown 3 (3/1/0) + label 1" (map/aerial) or "shown 2 (2/1/0) + named 2"
(outline map); options are aspects (3 @ 20 or 4 @ 15, select to benefit) up
to 60 plus Overall Coherence graded 20/17/14/10/6/0. Every task total equals
the paper's printed tariff ([8m], [20m], [30m], [80m]) and the scheme's own
split where it prints one ([16m] + [4m] for 9A and 10A).

Examiner annotation tables (REF/I/N/Ex/Dg icons) restate allocations already
printed above them and are not carried into guidance.

Boundaries follow the published allocation: at Ordinary Level the scheme
prices every printed roman of every A, B and C part (e.g. 1C (i) 3m + 3m,
(ii) 3m, (iii) 7 SRPs @ 3m), so each roman is its own task. Part One romans
and lettered true/false items are tasks; a matching or location table under
ONE printed instruction stays one task with a criterion per scheme row (the
scheme's rows follow the printed table rows; each was checked against the
image: Q1 Inner core=D, Mantle=B, Crust=A, Outer core=C; Q4 Vent=D,
Crater=C, Ash Cloud=A, Magma chamber=B; Q5 Madeira=B, Baton Rouge=C, Port
Douglas=A, Sahara=D; Q9 Islamic World=B, Donegal County Council=D, Paris=E,
Sambre Meuse=A, Mediterranean=C; Q10 Isobar=B, high=C, warm front=A, low=D).
A part whose wording depends on an earlier part ("named in part (i) above",
"this multinational company") carries that earlier printed part in its stem.

Tariffs: an SRP is 3 marks at Ordinary Level; "a + b" lines are one criterion
with partial credit a; graded lines keep their printed grades; sketch items
are "showing 3 (3/1/0) + labelled 2"; 4A items are "named 2 + shown 4
(4/2/0)". Every question totals 10 (Part One) or 100 = 30 + 40 + 30 (Part
Two) as printed.

Wording: the paper wins where the scheme reprints it differently (1B
"labelled diagrams", 2B "with the aid of a diagram", 2A "Sea stack",
7B "Services and footloose industries.").
